Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `shouldThrowAnExceptionOnTruncatedEntries()` expects an `IOException` when reading a truncated tar entry from a tar archive file. The test iterates through entries using `TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry()` and copies their contents. The bug report mentions that `TarArchiveInputStream` silently finishes without throwing `IOException` on unexpected EOF.

The method `getNextTarEntry()` reads the next tar entry by first ensuring the previous entry is fully skipped, then reading a 512-byte record header using `getRecord()`. If `getRecord()` returns `null`, indicating EOF, it returns `null`.

`getRecord()` relies on `readRecord()` which attempts to read a full 512-byte record, but if fewer bytes are read, it returns `null`, signaling EOF. `getRecord()` then checks if the record is an EOF record (all zeros or null) and sets `hasHitEOF`. If EOF record detected, it calls `tryToConsumeSecondEOFRecord()` and `consumeRemainderOfLastBlock()`, then returns null.

`tryToConsumeSecondEOFRecord()` tries to read the second EOF record as per tar spec, else resets the stream if mark supported. `consumeRemainderOfLastBlock()` skips remaining bytes in current block.

The `skip()` method used in `getNextTarEntry()` to skip entry contents only skips up to the known entry size (`entrySize`). If the tar archive is truncated unexpectedly (actual bytes less than `entrySize`), `skip()` will silently skip fewer bytes but no exception is thrown, and EOF is reached prematurely.

Thus, when reading a truncated tar input, `getNextTarEntry()` eventually encounters an EOF record and returns `null` instead of throwing an exception for truncated content. The truncated tar file does not trigger `IOException` as the code assumes incomplete data manifests only as EOF and treats it silently instead of an error.

The root issue is that `TarArchiveInputStream` and particularly its `skip()` and `readRecord()` methods don't detect or report unexpected EOF or truncated tar entry data as an error. They silently handle partial reads and EOF which leads to the test not throwing the expected IOException.

This diagnosis aligns with the bug report summary of silent finish on unexpected EOF in compressed tar archives and the failed test verifying detection of truncated entries.

Suggested fix locations would be inside `TarArchiveInputStream.skip(long)`, `readRecord()`, and possibly `getNextTarEntry()` for entry data validation and strict EOF handling to throw IOException on unexpected EOF.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
